messages.body_plain:

On Monday, 22 May 2017 06:21:29 UTC-7, Juliet Luft wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I've been following the instructions in the sequenza usage example (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sequenza/vignettes/sequenza.pdf), and at the moment my analysis keeps failing at "3.3 Generate a seqz file".
> I'm able to generate the GC content file, and convert my bam file to pileup format, but once I attempt to generate the seqz file it runs for a while (sometimes up to half an hour, sometimes less than 5 minutes) before stopping and producing the error: "Something went wrong on the block counting!!"
>
> When looking at the output files, they all stop at different points on chromosome 1, and some of the fields seem incomplete, eg: the last ten lines of one example:
> chr1    42816708        G       12      12      1.0     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0
> chr1    42816709        G       12      12      1.0     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0
> chr1    42816710        G       12      12      1.0     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0
> chr1    42816711        C       10      12      1.2     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      C       .       0
> chr1    42816712        G       8       13      1.625   1.0     0       hom     66.0    13      G       .       0
> chr1    42816713        C       9       13      1.444   1.0     0       hom     66.0    13      C       .       0
> chr1    42816714        T       9       12      1.333   1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      T       .       0
> chr1    42816715        G       8       13      1.625   1.0     0       hom     66.0    13      G       .       0
> chr1    42816716        G       8       12      1.5     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0
> chr1    42816717        A       8       12      1.5     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      A       .       0
>
>
> When generating the pileups I output huge numbers of errors with some variation of: "[fai_fetch_seq] The sequence "chrEBV" not found", although when I look at the output the pileups themselves appear fine.
> Could there be an issue with the pileups when is affected the seqz conversion?
>
> And advice you could give would be very much appreciated.
> Thank you.
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Sophie,

there might be something wrong in on the mpileup files, you can try to look for lines with 0 coverage or similar issues.

I’ve recently released an improved version of sequenza-utils as a stand alone python library.
In the new version I rewrote the pileup parser, this may solve your issue and if not, we can find out the problem and fix it :).

I suggest you to install samtools and tabix >=1.3 (1.2 may be good as well) and the newer sequenza-utils.

if you have a unix based system you should not have too much problem:

    pip install sequenza-utils

if you don’t have the pip command you can try to use other approaches

https://bitbucket.org/sequenza_tools/sequenza-utils

when the package is installed you can run from the command line:

   sequenza-utils

similarly to the python script provided in the R sequenza package, although pileup2seqz is now merged with bam2seqz (you need to run it with the --piileup flag)

If you decide to try the new sequenza-utils, it would be great if you could give some feedback.. positive or negative :)

If this doesn’t fix the problem please send me more details on the error (eg the lines of the pileup where the process stops)
and I should be able to fix the code and update the version in the python repository.

Francesco

> Thanks for trying this function. sequenza2PyClone was meant to be an experimental feature, I never tested it extensively.
